clue.text: Brahms and Liszt — initially with German king

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the two composers' names

parts.note: first letter of the composer's name
first letter of the other composer's name
Otto was the name of several German kings and emperors

explanation.surface: A note on two great composers and their link with a German monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Brahms and Liszt is Cockney rhyming slang for 'pissed', so the composers do double duty: as the definition and as the source of two initials.
explanation.definitionFit: In rhyming slang the composers' names stand for being drunk, which is what this slang word for very intoxicated means.

clue.text: President with term of endearment for tree-hugger

parts.note: either of the two US presidents called Bush
a pet name for a loved one
joins the two pieces

explanation.surface: A US president uses an affectionate nickname for an environmental campaigner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tree-hugger' suggests an eco-activist, but here it is literal: an animal that clings to branches.
explanation.definitionFit: The bushbaby, or galago, is a small African primate that lives in trees and clings to their branches.

clue.text: Keep an eye on poems in Old English

indicators.note: in places the poems inside the abbreviation for the old language

parts.note: standard abbreviation for Old English
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: A scholar monitors a collection of Anglo-Saxon poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: To supervise is to keep watch over, a synonym phrase for this verb.

clue.text: Blemished hotel covered by awful red stain

indicators.note: covered by means the hotel sits inside, wrapped by the other letters
something awful is in a bad state, so the letters are jumbled out of their proper order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hotel's reputation is spoiled by a nasty red mark.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of the red stain is TARNISED, with the H slipped in to give TARNISHED.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarnished means discoloured or sullied, a synonym of marred or spoiled in appearance.

clue.text: Angry start of barking? Armorer might make a bolt for it

definitions.text: Armorer might make a bolt for it

parts.note: cross means annoyed
a dog's bark is written bow-wow, and this is its first half

explanation.surface: An irritated dog and an armourer making a run for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start of barking' tempts you to take a B; the question mark points to the first part of bow-wow instead. 'Make a bolt' sounds like fleeing, but a bolt is the short arrow this weapon shoots.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbow is a medieval weapon that fires bolts, so an armourer would make the bolts as ammunition for it.

clue.text: Play, for example, we hear, with appropriate set

definitions.text: Play, for example, we hear, with appropriate set

parts.words: Play, for example, we hear, with appropriate set
parts.note: surface reading: a theatre review of a play, with a fitting stage set

parts.words: Play, for example, we hear, with appropriate set
parts.note: setter's reading: a drama that is listened to rather than watched, needing the right receiving set to pick it up

explanation.walkthrough: 'We hear' looks like a sound-alike signal but is literal: this play is only heard. 'Set' is not scenery but the receiver you tune in with.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama transmitted over the airwaves is heard by listeners with a wireless receiver, the kind of programme the phrase names.

clue.text: Call that's close — nothing in it

indicators.note: in it tells us the zero goes inside the word for close

parts.note: to close is to shut
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A narrow decision that turned out to be empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' reads as an adjective (a close call) but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To call out loudly is to yell, so the verb and the noun both fit this synonym.

clue.text: Not worthy of hospital, after instruction to avoid untidiness

indicators.note: after says the hospital letter is placed at the end, following the instruction

parts.note: an order to keep things tidy: be neat
H is the map and road-sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A hospital patient is told to stop being messy, which seems beneath them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beneath you is unworthy of your dignity, as in 'it's beneath him to complain'.

clue.text: What's wrong about part of our navy showing friendliness

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the rearranged letters surround the naval unit
wrong means out of order, so the letters of the first word must be rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange, without the 's
the Royal Marines are part of Britain's Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A complaint about a naval unit's surprisingly cordial behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of What's is just 'is' and not part of the fodder; WATH wraps the RM.
explanation.definitionFit: Warmth of manner is cordiality and kindness, a synonym of friendliness.

clue.text: Badly ruining one team sport for upwardly mobile types

indicators.note: doing something badly messes it up, so the following letters are scrambled

parts.note: the fourteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone is doing a poor job of wrecking a single team in a sport for social climbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upwardly mobile' usually means socially ambitious; here it means literally climbing upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbing peaks is a sport whose participants move upward, the literal sense of the social-climber phrase.

clue.text: E.g. bloody weapon put over wardrobe

indicators.note: put over means set around and covering, so the weapon encloses the clothing

parts.note: a sword is a bladed weapon
wear means clothing, as in evening wear, the contents of a wardrobe

explanation.surface: A bloodstained weapon has been laid on top of a wardrobe.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of the weapon stays in front and WEAR goes in after it. 'Bloody' is a British mild expletive, not a description of the sword.
explanation.definitionFit: In British speech bloody is a classic mild expletive, an example of a curse.

clue.text: Person who has minimal basic education about West

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the education phrase is wrapped around the compass point

parts.note: the basics of schooling are the three Rs; the minimum is one R
W is the compass abbreviation for west

explanation.surface: Someone with only the bare minimum of schooling is described in relation to the West.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic; one R is the least of them.
explanation.definitionFit: An owner is the possessor of something, literally the person in possession of it.

clue.text: Improperly obtains part of castle that's outstanding?

indicators.note: improperly means not in the correct manner, so the letters must be put in a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone acquires a magnificent piece of a castle by dishonest means.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' means excellent on the surface but literally standing out: a bastion juts out from the walls.
explanation.definitionFit: A bastion is a fortification that projects outward from a castle's main wall, so it literally stands out.

clue.text: Survive, like person asked to turn off light?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to live longer than

definitions.text: like person asked to turn off light?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read as two words: the person leaving the building at the end, who is asked to switch the lights off

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into OUT LAST: the last one out turns off the lights.
explanation.definitionFit: To outlast is to endure longer than another; the split phrase describes being the final person to leave.

clue.text: Source of mast that's come ashore, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word is taken by its sound when spoken, not its spelling

parts.note: to beach is to run a boat up onto the shore

explanation.surface: A ship's mast that has washed up on the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: Mast here is not a ship's pole but the nuts that fall from forest trees, used as pig feed.
explanation.definitionFit: Beech mast is the fallen nuts of the beech tree, so the tree is the source of that mast.

clue.text: Correctly wrapping parts of it separately, beyond doubt

indicators.note: wrapping means enclosing, so the two letters of the pronoun go inside the adverb
separately says the two letters are not kept together but slotted in at different points

parts.note: aright means correctly
the two letters of 'it', inserted one at a time

explanation.surface: Handling each section of something properly leaves no room for doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Separately' means the I and T go in at two different points: I after the A, T after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: An airtight case or alibi is one with no flaws or gaps, idiomatically leaving no room for question.

clue.text: Usually popular military leader

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a general is a senior army officer

explanation.surface: A well-liked army commander, as is normally the case.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means as a rule or on the whole, a synonym of usually.

clue.text: Navigational aid provided by some Europeans sailor follows

indicators.note: follows says the sailor comes after the Europeans in the answer

parts.note: people from Poland
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A navigation device supplied by a group of European sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Polaris, the pole star, sits almost directly above the North Pole and has long guided sailors' navigation.

clue.text: Fish restricted area around island, one in Med

indicators.note: restricted means cut short, so the fish loses its final letter

parts.note: a sardine is a small fish

indicators.note: around means turned about, so area and island are read in the opposite order

parts.note: standard abbreviation for area
standard abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A no-fishing zone has been set up around an island in the Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Restricted area' looks like one phrase, but restricted belongs to the fish. 'One in Med' is the definition: one island in the Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: Sardinia is a large Italian island in the Mediterranean Sea, an example of an island there.

clue.text: Highly moving letters from survivor he heard

indicators.note: heard means the words are taken by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: an heir survives the person whose estate they inherit
he denotes a male

explanation.surface: Deeply touching letters from someone who survived, he was told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highly moving' sounds emotional, but means travelling high up, by aeroplane.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmail is post carried by aircraft, so the letters literally travel high in the sky.

clue.text: Enjoyment from third of August onward to first of October

indicators.note: from third onward means everything before the third letter of the month is dropped

parts.note: the month whose first two letters go; that its tail runs on into 'onward' is coincidence

indicators.note: first of picks only the opening letter of the next month's name

parts.note: opening letter of the month

explanation.surface: Pleasure lasting from the third of August through to the first of October.
explanation.walkthrough: The dates are a disguise: 'third of August onward' means the month from its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is hearty enjoyment or relish, as in eating with gusto.

clue.text: Ostentatious when receiving royalty? It's not always clear

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the ostentatious word holds the royal abbreviation

parts.note: showy means flashy or ostentatious
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: Someone shows off when entertaining royals, though their motives are murky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clear' suggests clear meaning; it is clear weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Showery weather has intermittent rain, so the sky is clear only some of the time.

clue.text: Observes a weight go up and down

parts.note: to observe is to see
taken as written
W is the abbreviation for weight

explanation.surface: Someone watches a weight rise and fall.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, seesaw means to move alternately up and down, like a child's teeter-totter.

clue.text: Problem with hearing organ — people finally are dispersed round a church

indicators.note: dispersed means split apart, and round means the split word goes around what follows
finally points to the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: last letter of the word
taken as written, then split
taken as written
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A congregation's hearing trouble: everyone scatters around the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dispersed' looks like an anagram signal, but here the word is merely broken in two, its halves either side of the church, with no letters reordered.
explanation.definitionFit: Earache is pain in the ear, a complaint affecting the organ of hearing.

clue.text: Look into prisoner that may be part way through sentence

definitions.text: that may be part way through sentence

indicators.note: into means the first word is put inside the second

parts.note: con is slang for a convict
lo is an old word for look, as in lo and behold

explanation.surface: An inquiry into a convict who may be halfway through his jail term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sentence' suggests prison time, which the prisoner reinforces; it is the grammatical sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A colon is a punctuation mark that can appear midway in a written sentence, introducing a list or explanation.

clue.text: In a word, suggest piece of music to study first

indicators.note: first means the study word is placed at the front, before the music

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn by heart
a note is a single musical sound

explanation.surface: Briefly, someone recommends learning a musical piece before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a word' looks like 'in short', but it qualifies the definition: words connote meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To connote is to imply something beyond a word's literal meaning, so a word suggests an idea.

clue.text: Intend to silence everyone

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Someone plans to quieten everybody in the room.
explanation.definitionFit: The modal verb expresses future intention, as in 'I shall go', a determination to act.

clue.text: Revolutionary, ensuring changes ahead of time

indicators.note: ahead of says the rearranged letters come before the time abbreviation
changes means is altered, so the preceding word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A revolutionary making sure that change arrives early.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurgent is a rebel fighting against established authority, a synonym of revolutionary as a noun.

clue.text: Almost spring and time for play? Almost

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the second word loses its last letter

parts.note: a well is a spring of water
evening is when plays are put on, as in opening night

explanation.surface: Spring is nearly here, and with it the time for games.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word sits at both ends: the first 'Almost' is the definition, the last one is the signal to shorten.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-nigh is an old-fashioned phrase meaning very nearly, a synonym of practically.

clue.text: Musician with piano accompanying film

parts.note: P is the musical marking for piano, meaning softly
a film is a thin layer, as of dust
joins the two pieces side by side

explanation.surface: A musician at the piano providing music for a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' suggests a movie; it is a thin coating.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is someone who performs on an instrument, a synonym of musician.
